description: Portable processor scenarios for the OpenAPI 3.2 binding-specification sibling. Configuration is named semantically; adapters normalize HTTP observations.

scenarios.description: The exact 3.2.0 edition is admitted, an operation with omitted responses remains addressable, and the plain empty unary response uses the explicit 3.1-equivalence bridge.
A later patch-looking 3.2 edition is refused at the exact pre-resolution edition gate.
The 3.2 family token does not infer acceptance of a 3.1 artifact.
Selector evaluation never percent-decodes an RFC 6901 path segment.
Root $self establishes the OpenAPI-description base used by a relative selected Path Item reference.
A selected reference that uses a retrieval alias despite the target document's declared $self identity is excluded before dispatch.
A Path Item $ref collision on the selected method excludes that target.
A collision confined to an unused Path Item method does not exclude the selected operation.
Omitting components, paths, and webhooks leaves no possible target position and refuses the whole source after the closed load gates without becoming a fifth load gate.
A root jsonSchemaDialect outside the incorporated base dialect excludes the whole source, including a schema-free target.
A present empty Responses Object excludes the selected target while omission remains addressable.
Reference identity applies through the selected request closure: a Request Body reference using a retrieval alias instead of the target document's $self identity is excluded.
A selected Schema Object reference cannot cross a nearer $id resource boundary using the containing OpenAPI document plus a deep pointer.

A response-only reference-identity divergence does not leak into M5's request gate; the empty unary response remains on the explicit equivalence bridge and the divergent response cell is deferred to M6.
An unsupported $schema at a selected schema-resource root excludes the selected operation while the source itself remains admitted.
A duplicate YAML mapping key refuses at the accepted-representation grammar gate.
A multi-document YAML stream refuses because exactly one document is admitted.
A YAML value with no JSON data-model image refuses at the compatibility gate.
A non-object root refuses at the closed root-shape load gate.
An object root without the required string openapi field refuses at edition discrimination.
An unusable root $self does not fall back semantically to the retrieval URI for a selected relative reference.
An unresolvable reference confined to an unused sibling operation does not destroy the selected target.
A resolvable cyclic Schema Object graph terminates reference traversal and remains usable.
The fixed query field dispatches the uppercase QUERY method, and QUERY carries its declared request content as the query operation rather than deleting it as GET-like content.
An additionalOperations key retains its exact authored capitalization in both selector identity and the HTTP method sent on the wire.
Additional-operation lookup is byte-exact, so a case-changed selector names no operation and never dispatches.
An additionalOperations map key containing a slash is not an HTTP token even when the selector escapes that map-key segment exactly.
An additionalOperations key comparing ASCII-case-insensitively equal to the fixed query field is excluded as its own entry.
A colliding additional-operation entry does not exclude the distinct fixed QUERY operation on the same Path Item.
RFC 6901 escaping applies once to an additional method key, so F~0O selects and dispatches the exact F~O HTTP token.
Selector evaluation resolves a referenced Path Item before reading an additionalOperations entry and composes a non-colliding adjacent entry.
The same additional-operation key in a referenced and adjacent Path Item is an undefined selected-field collision and excludes that target.
A Path Item $ref collision confined to an unused additional-operation key does not exclude a different selected additional operation.
A TRACE requestBody declaration creates no required caller body and a body-free invocation dispatches TRACE without content.
A supplied caller body on TRACE is unroutable and refuses before dispatch even when the artifact declares requestBody.
The caller correspondence is closed to parameters and body, so an unknown top-level key refuses before dispatch.
A present caller-envelope parameters member must be an object and refuses before dispatch otherwise.
Cross-location same-name parameters activate qualified mode for every parameter and remain independently writable through location/RFC6901-name keys.
Once cross-location duplication activates qualified mode, the bare parameter name is unknown and refuses before dispatch.
A present body member carrying JSON null is supplied rather than absent and crosses the correspondence boundary as the one JSON null body value.
Omission of a required request body remains distinct from supplied null and refuses before dispatch.
An unknown key inside the parameters object refuses before dispatch; no unmatched-field passthrough exists even without a body.
A form-urlencoded querystring Parameter supplies the complete raw query component; its authored parameter name is not serialized and the result receives no second escaping pass.
A non-urlencoded JSON querystring representation is percent-encoded as one complete query component with uppercase percent triplets.
An operation-level querystring Parameter colliding with an ordinary query Parameter inherited from its Path Item excludes the target before input inspection.
More than one effective querystring Parameter across Path Item and Operation owners excludes the selected target.
A querystring Parameter with an explicitly present schema-form field is excluded even when that field equals its typed default.
A whole null in the matrix path cell serializes as the name-only matrix segment ;id.
A whole null in the label path cell serializes as the label prefix alone.
A whole null in the simple path cell serializes as the empty string.
Whole null values in the form query and cookie cells serialize as present empty name=value contributions.
A whole null in the spaceDelimited query cell is n/a and refuses before dispatch.
A null member inside an array has no RFC 6570 representation and refuses before dispatch.
deepObject ignores an explicit explode false value and emits its brackets percent-encoded exactly as the 3.2 style example.
Manual allowReserved query construction still percent-encodes square brackets, fragment, query-pair, equals, and plus delimiters while retaining other permitted reserved bytes.
The pipeDelimited query separator is emitted as uppercase %7C rather than a raw non-RFC-6570 delimiter.
The 3.2 cookie style admits repeated array pairs and gives whole null its defined empty value, joined by the RFC 6265 semicolon-space separator.
Omission of a required non-path Parameter refuses before dispatch on the 3.2 lane.
A style-location cell outside the closed 3.2 table excludes the selected target before caller values are inspected.
A resolved object member that is itself compound has no defined style expansion and statically excludes the target.
An effective path Parameter without a matching template expression excludes the target under exact one-to-one correspondence.
A path-template expression appearing more than once violates exact one-to-one correspondence and excludes the target.
Two templated path keys with an equivalent static hierarchy are ambiguous and exclude either selected target.
A JSON content-form query Parameter serializes first and then percent-encodes that entire representation as one value.
A querystring media entry with itemSchema selects a sequential representation and excludes the target because a stream has no query-component mapping.
Supplying both a raw Cookie Header Parameter and a structured cookie Parameter refuses before dispatch rather than merging them.
A form-style exploded cookie whose resolved array declaration always produces multiple cookie pairs is statically excluded.
A supplied JSON number on a schema-form Parameter refuses when parameterConversion is not configured; no canonical spelling is inferred.
allowEmptyValue true preserves a supplied empty query string as a present empty name=value pair.
A querystring Parameter sharing its name with a Header Parameter activates qualified mode and each location remains independently writable.
Exactly one usable concrete request media entry self-selects, strict JSON rides as UTF-8, and the 3.2 request lane emits no Accept header.
Two usable concrete request alternatives require requestMedia before input consumption; the supplied value never elects one.
A concrete requestMedia value matching two declarations at equal exact-and-parameter specificity refuses instead of using map order.
An absent optional body bypasses a multi-alternative request media map and emits neither body nor Content-Type.
text/json is character data rather than JSON and carries a sole-string declaration without adding JSON quotes.
A boolean non-JSON text value serializes as exactly true under its declaration-selected character lane.
A non-JSON text number uses the shortest exact spelling, preferring 1e3 over the longer non-exponent 1000.
A supplied null on the nullable-string character lane refuses because that lane defines no null lexical form.
A schema-omitted concrete non-JSON body uses canonical Base64 at the OpenBindings boundary and dispatches the decoded octets.
A non-canonical raw-octet boundary string with missing Base64 padding refuses before dispatch.
A sole-string declaration with contentEncoding carries the artifact-encoded characters unchanged rather than Base64-decoding them.
An object-valued XML alternative is excluded because the incorporated authority does not determine all XML bytes.
Explicit allowReserved false is still field presence: it selects the form style path, ignores contentType, and spells a space as percent-20 rather than plus.
A name-based Encoding key with no corresponding property is ignored and does not disturb the declared property.
A name-based multipart array emits one part per item in order under the repeated property name.
A string part with contentEncoding remains artifact text and emits the equivalent Content-Transfer-Encoding header.
An explicit part transfer Header that disallows the schema contentEncoding excludes that field and refuses an invocation that reaches it.
Positional multipart emits one part per array item in order, applying prefixEncoding by position and itemEncoding to the remainder.
Name-based encoding combined with positional itemEncoding invalidates only that multipart alternative; a JSON sibling remains selectable.
Positional multipart/form-data refuses when the applicable Encoding Object has no fixed Content-Disposition name.
A Content-Disposition Header default does not fix a positional form-data part name; only const or a single-member enum does.
One active nested Encoding level recursively serializes an array property as a multipart/mixed part containing its ordered items.
An alternative requiring more than one nested Encoding level is unavailable and refuses when it is the only request representation.
A JSON Lines request consumes one caller array and emits one JSON item per line while allowing schema and itemSchema to coexist.
A +json-seq request frames each JSON item with record separator and line feed in array order.
text/event-stream is excluded on requests because incorporated authority supplies no object-to-event write algorithm.
itemSchema on a media type with no incorporated sequential framing excludes only that request alternative rather than treating it as ordinary JSON.
A components.mediaTypes reference resolves before positional multipart lane selection, and its raw Encoding overlay remains attached to the selected artifact.
A typeless form-urlencoded property takes its application/octet-stream default, decodes the canonical Base64 boundary, and percent-encodes the resulting octets.
A typeless name-based multipart property uses the raw-octet lane and its application/octet-stream part default.
A wildcard Encoding contentType requires one concrete propertyMedia choice for the affected property before input consumption.
A concrete propertyMedia choice matching a wildcard Encoding member fixes the part Content-Type without changing that property's raw-octet boundary.
A supplied null optional property on the content-based form path is elided while unaffected sibling fields remain.
A required nullable content-based form property cannot be silently elided; a supplied null therefore refuses before dispatch.
Encoding, prefixEncoding, and itemEncoding are ignored on application/json even when their nested contents would be unavailable on multipart.
Nested Encoding fields are ignored when their governing part Content-Type is explicitly non-multipart.
A concrete requestMedia choice materializes the 3.2 runtime-type non-JSON text lane through a declared media range.
A concrete requestMedia choice materializes JSON Lines framing and itemSchema through a declared media range.
An absent optional body bypasses request media planning even when its only authored alternative has no request write algorithm.

OAS 3.2.0 §§4.14.3.1, 4.14.4, and 4.14.6.3 require ordered per-item processing for sequential media and model each parsed text/event-stream item as the applicable data/event/id/retry object. This seed uses the edition's worked SSE bytes and equivalent JSON records [CO32-12, CO32-13].
